title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: How does the idempotency wrapper of a rest-crud create or patch join the store's write transaction, with its tenant and principal?
description: ST-SUP-RC30-OC04 and OC05 say that the wrapper call that the idempotency component emits claims the key row, runs the handler and completes the row inside the store's write transaction, scoped by tenant, principal and key, and OC01 says that the OpenAPI document carries the Idempotency-Key header on the POST and PATCH operations. On main this cannot be built from the idempotency component: the create and patch handlers of rest-api (ST-SUP-RC20) call Create and Patch of the GORM store (ST-SUP-RC01), and each store method opens and commits its own transaction, so no generated code outside the store reaches that transaction; the one transaction the store gives a callback, WithTransaction, is SERIALIZABLE, but idempotency.Wrap needs READ COMMITTED, because its SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT must see a key row that another transaction committed after this one began; the verified identity of the generated service carries no tenant (ST-SUP-RC20-OC35 and the tenancy component ST-SUP-RC27 are not built, see ST-SUP-Q64); and only rest-api writes the OpenAPI document, and gen.Wiring gives another component no way to add a header parameter or a problem response to an operation. Declared commands are not affected: command.Run already calls the wrapper (ST-SUP-RP10-LC11). Options: (A) rest-api runs each operation that Required on names in one store write transaction: the PostgreSQL adapter emits a store method that opens the transaction through tenant.Begin at READ COMMITTED and gives the callback the transaction and a store bound to it; the idempotency component emits, for each such operation, its settings (required or accepted, the retention, the problem type URIs under the problem base) and its fingerprint function over the fields the operation declares, and the handler of rest-api calls idempotency.Wrap with them inside that transaction and records its own response for the wrapper; rest-api reads the idempotency setting from gen.Context and adds the header and the 400, 409 and 422 responses to its OpenAPI document; the tenant comes as ST-SUP-Q64 decides. (B) A rest-crud create and patch become commands of the command capability (ST-SUP-RC32) served by command.Run, which already wraps; the idempotency component then emits only the per-operation settings, fingerprint functions, OpenAPI parameters and conformance tests. This waits on ST-SUP-Q60, ST-SUP-Q61 and the runtime store of ST-SUP-Q64 option (c). (C) The idempotency component emits an HTTP middleware that opens its own READ COMMITTED transaction and puts it in the request context, and every store method of the PostgreSQL adapter uses a transaction from the context when there is one. Recommendation: (A), because the store keeps the one transaction and its isolation, it is the path that ST-SUP-Q64 option (a) recommends for tenant.Begin, and it needs no change to the runtime; (C) hides the transaction in the context, and (B) waits on three open questions. Until this is decided, the idempotency builder stops OC01, OC04, OC05 and OC06; OC02 and OC03 (the problem type URIs and the fingerprint functions) do not depend on it.
